title: Fractal deconfinement and confinement in Sierpinski ice
abstract: We study the six-vertex model on the Sierpinski gasket, a four-coordinated hierarchical fractal with Hausdorff dimension $d_f=\log_23$. Given the importance of dimensionality for the long-wavelength behavior of such models, we specifically consider correlations and confinement as a function of the vertex weights, with the equal-weight point corresponding to the ice model. We calculate the partition function and correlators recursively to obtain a rich phase diagram hosting many different regimes. While the ice model shows entropic charge confinement, a particular four-vertex limit exhibits fractal deconfinement, with the string joining the deconfined charges itself a statistical fractal with fractal dimension $d_l=\log_2(5/2)\approx 1.3$. Finally, we propose a setup as an artificial spin ice to enable experimental study of the rich phenomenology of Sierpinski ice and its generalisations.
summary: This paper analyzes the six-vertex model on the Sierpinski gasket fractal to study charge confinement. It finds that while the standard ice limit shows confinement, specific parameter choices lead to a novel 'fractal deconfinement' regime. The work uses recursive calculations to determine key observables like string tension and the fractal dimension of the connecting strings.
main_problem: The study investigates fractal deconfinement and confinement phenomena by analyzing statistical mechanical models on fractal lattices.
main_result: The model exhibits a transition from entropic charge confinement (in the ice limit) to fractal deconfinement in specific parameter regimes, characterized by a non-trivial string dimension $d_l$.
method: The authors employ recursive calculations for partition functions and correlators tailored to the hierarchical structure of the Sierpinski gasket.
model_or_system: The system is the six-vertex model applied to the Sierpinski gasket, a four-coordinated fractal with Hausdorff dimension $d_f=\log_2 3$. The analysis compares regimes like the standard ice point to specific low-energy limits (e.g., HAFM).
key_observables: String tension ($	au$), correlation decay length ($\xi$), and the fractal dimension of the connecting string ($d_l$).
important_parameters: The vertex weights (x, y, z) which define different regimes; the fractal dimension $d_f = \log_2 3$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on deriving and solving coupled recurrence relations based on the hierarchical structure of the lattice.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate recursion relation flows, phase diagrams showing parameter dependence, and geometric representations of string paths with different fractal dimensions ($d_l$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the model on the fractal, deriving recursive relations for partition functions, analyzing how correlations decay (confinement vs. deconfinement), and finally proposing experimental realizations using artificial spin ice.
why_interesting: The concept of emergent fractional dimensions ($d_l$) governing topological excitations (strings) in a statistical system provides deep insights into how dimensionality affects long-range order, relevant to understanding critical phenomena in complex materials.
